headline: England beat Panama 2-0 to top Group L, Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane shine
summary: England secured their spot atop Group L with a 2-0 victory over Panama, thanks to crucial goals from Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane. This win ensures a smoother path through the World Cup knockout phase.
details: Jude Bellingham led England to a 2-0 victory over Panama, scoring one goal and assisting another for Harry Kane. This win secured England's position at the top of Group L, allowing them to avoid a challenging route in the World Cup knockout phase.

After a goalless first half and a frustrating hour of dominant possession, Bellingham broke the deadlock in the 62nd minute. He skillfully stabbed a left-footed finish past the goalkeeper from a crowded box following a corner.

Just five minutes later, Bellingham set up Kane, who headed home to double England's lead. This marked Kane's 11th World Cup goal for England, surpassing Gary Lineker's record and making him the country's all-time leading scorer in World Cups.

The victory transformed the mood at the New York New Jersey Stadium, with anxious supporters quickly shifting to celebratory singing. England finished the group stage with seven points, ahead of Croatia, while Panama lost all three matches.

Manager Thomas Tuchel had made five changes to the squad, including resting Declan Rice and bringing in more attack-minded players. Jordan Henderson also made history by becoming the first England player to participate in four World Cups.

headline_marked: [[Vlasic header sends Croatia into World Cup knockouts]] with 2-1 win over Ghana in Group L
headline: Vlasic header sends Croatia into World Cup knockouts with 2-1 win over Ghana in Group L
summary: Nikola Vlasic's 83rd-minute header secured a crucial 2-1 victory for Croatia over Ghana, ensuring their second-place finish in World Cup Group L and a spot in the last 32.
details: Nikola Vlasic scored an 83rd-minute header from a Luka Modric corner, lifting Croatia to a 2-1 victory over Ghana. This win secured Croatia's second-place finish in World Cup Group L.
The decisive goal came 10 minutes after Derrick Luckassen had equalized for Ghana on his international debut. Luckassen's goal was subject to a lengthy VAR review before being confirmed as onside.
Petar Susic had given Croatia a deserved lead after 31 minutes with a long-range strike into the bottom left corner. Croatia only needed a draw to advance to the last 32.

As Group L runners-up, Croatia will now face the second-placed team from Group K, likely Portugal or Colombia, in Toronto on Thursday. Ghana, who finished third, will meet the Group K winners in Kansas City on Friday.

Ghana showed significant improvement in the second half, with Luckassen's 73rd-minute goal being their first shot on target. Despite a late ankle injury scare for Antoine Semenyo, he was able to complete the match.
